page: Microsoft Azure M96bds_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the MBDSMediumMemoryv3 family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8473C processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, delivering 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Operating at a clock speed of 4.0 GHz, the CPU features a 105 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The server is equipped with 768.0 GB of RAM, providing a 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio, and includes 410 GB of local storage with premium block storage capabilities.

Benchmark data reveals top-tier memory and multi-core processing performance. The server achieves top-tier status in memory bandwidth tests for both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks, alongside top-tier multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Geekbench multi-core scores. Single-core performance is average to strong, while Passmark database operations and static web serving throughput rank in the top tier. The hardware-assisted matrix and vector extensions contribute to strong performance in LLM prompt processing and text generation across small, medium, and large models.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the M96bds_v3 offers high resource density, combining substantial memory capacity with dedicated high-frequency compute resources. While single-core CPU benchmarks sit in the average tier, the massive multi-core throughput and top-tier memory bandwidth offset this for parallelized workloads. The lack of a GPU limits its utility for heavy deep learning training, but its high memory-to-core ratio and strong database performance make it highly suitable for large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, enterprise ERP applications, and memory-intensive data processing pipelines.
